findings.message: ruleItems() turns any failure to count a rule's rows into 0 with `.catch(() => 0)`. A rule that fails (missing column, bad subject cast, timeout) is dropped from the inventory. erase() only applies rules that appear in the inventory, so the request completes as 'Erased' while that table still holds the person's data. The person is never told and neither is the approver. Fix: record the item as 'could not check' and refuse to open or complete the request until every rule could be counted.
findings.scenario: time.entry subject `user_id` fails to cast in the count → item missing → complete_privacy_request reports done and subject_label='Erased person' while time.entry.note still holds the person's notes

findings.message: Erasure finds rows only through `subject` columns that hold the person's ids. Several new entries keep the person's name but have no subject column that names the person. presales.activity, presales.task, presales.risk and presales.suggestion have no subject at all. delivery.proposal's subject is `project_id` but the personal field is owner_name. These rows never appear in an access or erasure inventory, and the request still completes as erased. Fix: give each name-bearing table a subject column for the person (an owner_user_id or actor id), or fail the standard when `fields` hold a personal value that `subject` can't reach.
findings.scenario: Erasure request for Rizwan, who owns presales tasks and a proposal → request completes; presales.task.owner_name and delivery.proposal.owner_name still read 'Rizwan Farook', and his access package leaves them out

findings.message: privacyOverview sums only `preview.counts` and ignores `preview.failed`. A rule whose preview fails reads as 0 in 'Due tonight' and in the lede ('Tonight's purge removes N records'). Nothing on screen says the rule couldn't be checked. Fix: return the failed rules and show them as unknown or needing attention.
findings.scenario: A retention rule names a column that doesn't exist → previewPurge logs and skips it → the ticket shows 'Due tonight 0' and the nightly purge fails NonRetryable

findings.message: 'Data classes covered' is hard-coded as `${rules} of ${rules}` with progress 100% and 'Every personal-data table has a rule'. It counts the rules against themselves, so it can never show a gap. Fix: compare against the personal-data tables found (the check-module-standard scan, or a declared inventory), or drop the claim.
findings.scenario: A module's personal table has no retention entry → the ticket still says '20 of 20, every personal-data table has a rule'

findings.message: Chat retention is declared as `period: P90D, start: { at: [], idle: P90D }`. due() computes `updated_at < now() - idle - period`, so a conversation is purged only after 180 idle days. The label and TENANT_DEFAULTS say 'kept 90 days after its last message'. Fix: `start: { at: ['updated_at'] }` or `idle: 'P0D'`.
findings.scenario: A conversation whose last message was 120 days ago → the purge leaves it in place, though the screen says it is kept for 90 days

findings.message: The privacy source list is hand-built twice: here and in scripts/seed-demo.ts (the test builds a third copy). Both copies leave out apiPlatform, so the `api.rate_limited` retention rule is invisible to the purge, legal holds, set_retention_period and the screen. packages/api/src/module.ts then enforces it with its own hard-coded `api.prune` deletes, which also delete api.inbound and api.delivery without a declared rule. Those deletes ignore legal holds and tenant overrides, which is exactly what 032 replaced workflows.prune for. Fix: derive the sources from the same manifest list as jobs and workflows, including api, and remove the hard-coded deletes in favour of retention entries.
findings.scenario: Admin runs set_retention_period for the rate-limit log at P1Y → 'no retention rule'; and api.prune still deletes at 90 days while a legal hold is active

findings.message: [design] The SSRF guard on outgoing webhook URLs only checks the hostname text against a regex, and only when the webhook is subscribed. It does not resolve the hostname. It also misses whole classes of private addresses: internal DNS names (k3s `*.svc.cluster.local`, `metadata.google.internal`), wildcard DNS that points at private IPs (`127.0.0.1.nip.io`), `0.0.0.0`, IPv4-mapped IPv6 (`[::ffff:7f00:1]`), CGNAT 100.64/10, and decimal or octal IP forms. `deliver.ts` `post()` then calls `fetch` on the stored URL without checking again, so DNS rebinding also works. amax is a multi-tenant SaaS, so any tenant's Admin gets a signed blind POST into the provider's internal network. Fix: resolve the host at delivery time and reject private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT and mapped ranges on the resolved address (pin the connection to that address). Keep the subscribe-time check as a first filter only.
findings.scenario: subscribe_webhook url=https://amax-web.default.svc.cluster.local/api/jobs/tick → publicHttps returns true → every event the tenant emits is POSTed to the internal service

findings.message: Replay protection for GitHub and amax-signed calls rests on dedupe by `x-github-delivery` / `x-amax-delivery`. Those headers are not covered by the signature. GitHub sends no timestamp, and amax checks only the 5-minute window. A captured request replayed with a fresh delivery id passes the signature check and the dedupe. The screen still claims 'each event once'. Fix: dedupe on a hash of the signed body (as msgraph does) or include the id in the signed material.
findings.scenario: Replay a captured GitHub push with x-github-delivery set to a new UUID → receiveWebhook returns ok:true again and the event is processed twice

findings.message: Outgoing webhook masking guesses 002 classes from field names with its own regex list. That is a second copy of the sensitivity classification, and it disagrees with the modules' declared classes. For example, hr retention classes epf_number as `pay`, but classOf('epf_number') / classOf('epfNumber') is undefined. Pay data then goes unmasked to external receivers. Fix: mask from the emitting module's declared field classes, and fail closed on fields with no class.
findings.scenario: An event payload with { epfNumber: 'EPF-123' } → delivered to the webhook URL in clear text

findings.message: When the tenant has no secret configured for a provider, the call is recorded as reason 'missing', the same as a request with no signature. The screen then reports it as an 'unsigned webhook call rejected … claiming to be from X'. 'We could not verify' reads as 'attacker'. Fix: record a separate reason (not_configured) and show it as a setup problem.
findings.scenario: Tenant never stored azure-devops-webhook; a genuine ADO service hook arrives → the ticket counts it as a rejected unsigned call

findings.message: LIMITS hard-codes '120 a minute per token, 240 per person' and '600 a minute per person'. The real values come from rate-limit.ts defaults and the AMAX_RATE_* env overrides. The page notes also hard-code '5 failures' (MAX_FAILURES) and '5 minutes' (REPLAY_WINDOW_MS). Fix: render from the configured limits and constants.
findings.scenario: AMAX_RATE_CALL_TOKEN=60 → requests are limited at 60/min while the screen says 120

findings.message: The ✓auto retention check only parses lowercase `create table schema.t (` blocks that end with a line holding just `);`, plus `add column`. `CREATE TABLE`, `create table if not exists`, one-line tables and `alter table … add` without `column` are skipped silently, so the check passes. The manifest match is `includes('table: "x"')`, which a comment also satisfies. Fix: parse case-insensitively and with `if not exists`, and fail on migrations it can't parse.
findings.scenario: A migration with 'CREATE TABLE people.visit (id uuid, visitor_email text);' → the check reports no problem

findings.message: The duplicate-request check is a read followed by an insert, with no unique constraint, so two concurrent opens both succeed. Fix: add a partial unique index on (tenant_id, subject_user_id, kind) where status in ('open','approved').
findings.scenario: Two HR people open an erasure request for the same person at the same moment → two open requests

findings.message: twoPersonRule compares `ctx.actor.id` with `openedBy`, but openedBy and approved_by are written with personOf(ctx) (onBehalfOf ?? actor.id). The SQL gate compares approved_by with opened_by, so the two checks use different identities and can disagree. Compare personOf(ctx) in both.
The fixture derives subject_key with an unkeyed sha256(userId), while openPrivacyRequest uses keyed(userId). The demo row's key never matches one the service would compute. Use keyed().

Read tools always build their context with source 'chat' (`ctx = ctxFor(v, 'chat')`), even when called over MCP or the API, so trace and authorize see the wrong channel. Pass the tool's source through.
The 'Outgoing deliveries' note is the fixed string 'Nothing sent this week', even when deliveries exist and a percentage is shown. Make it conditional on stats.deliveries.total.
findings.scenario: 2,140 deliveries this week → the ticket shows 99.6% next to 'Nothing sent this week'

findings.message: The Settings hub's API card has a static chip ('Keys shown once') instead of a live status. A switched-off webhook or an expiring service credential doesn't surface on the attention-first hub. Derive the chip and attention text from apiStats and the credential list.

[design] A REST call made with a service credential runs the tool as the person it acts for. Admin tools build their ServiceContext with `ctxFor(viewer, source)`, which carries no principal. So the audited actor is `user:<person>` with kind `user`, and the credential (`sp:<id>`) appears only in the trace. This breaks AGENTS rule 4 (the record must say it was an agent or service acting for the person). It also defeats the two-person rule's check that a privacy request is completed by a person, not an agent or service (`twoPersonRule` checks `actor.kind !== 'user'`). The privacy write tools have no chat-only guard, unlike `create_api_credential`, so the erasure can run with no confirm card at all. Fix: carry the principal into the ServiceContext (`actor: sp:<id>`, kind `service`, `onBehalfOf: user:<id>`), and make `open/complete_privacy_request` chat-only the way `chatOnly()` does for credentials.
findings.scenario: An Admin creates a credential with scope admin:write that acts for an HR user → POST /api/v1/tools/complete_privacy_request {id} with amax-act-for=<HR user> → the erasure completes, the audit row says actor user:<HR> kind user, and nothing records that a CI key approved it

findings.message: [design] `completePrivacyRequest` builds the inventory from the merged ids (`req.subjects` plus the ids `resolveSubject` returns now). `erase()` applies the rules, and `privacy.erase_request` erases the audit and trace chains, using only the `req.subjects` stored when the request was opened. The legal-hold check also uses only the stored ids. Ids added since then (a new hr.person row, a resolver added by a newly installed module) are listed as erased but are never erased or checked against holds. Fix: write the merged ids back to `privacy.request.subjects` before calling `erase_request`, and use them for `about()` and the hold check.
findings.scenario: An erasure is opened for a user who has no hr.person row yet → HR creates the hr.person row → a second Admin completes the request → the inventory lists 'Leavers' HR record' but the `about(rule, req.subjects)` filter has no hr.person id, so the name and email stay, while the request says 'Erased person'

findings.message: [design] The proxy calls `takeRate` from its own copy of `@amax/core/rate-limit`. `configureRateLimits` runs only in `lib/server.ts` `getDb()`, inside the app's server bundle, and Next compiles the proxy as a separate entry, so module state is not shared. The page limiter therefore always uses the built-in defaults (AMAX_RATE_PAGE_* is ignored) and the no-op sink, so page 429s are never recorded in api.rate_limited and the 'Pages' row always shows 0. Fix: configure the limiter inside proxy.ts from `loadEnv()`, and give it a recorder or a shared store.
findings.scenario: AMAX_RATE_PAGE_USER=3 → the fourth navigation in a minute still loads; a user who hits 600 navigations gets 429, but the API and webhooks screen shows Pages: 0 limited

findings.message: [design] `apiRetention` (api.rate_limited, P90D) is declared, but `setPrivacySources` in lib/server.ts never includes `api()`. The rule never reaches the 032 catalog, the screen or `set_retention_period`. Meanwhile `api.prune` is a second, hard-coded retention path: raw deletes of api.rate_limited, api.inbound and api.delivery that ignore tenant periods and legal holds. That is exactly what architecture.md says 032 replaced `workflows.prune` to stop. Fix: register the api retention entries (including inbound and delivery) as privacy sources and delete `api.prune`.
findings.scenario: An HR person runs set_retention_period for 'api.rate_limited.subject' to P1Y → 'no retention rule'; at day 91, api.prune deletes the rows regardless of any setting
